cards.body:
## Summary
The annotation space is normalized per axis (x over width, y over height), but every distance core computes treats it as square. The video aspect sits in AnnotationDoc and PenEngine and never reaches the maths that needs it. Give normalized space one Metric (distances measured in content-width units, y scaled by 1/aspect) and route every distance through it.

## Description
One normalized unit of y is 0.5625 of one unit of x on a 16:9 picture. Core ignores that at 9 sites: PenEngine.distance (circle and spotlight radius), all five HitTest branches plus pointToSegment, Smoothing.decimate, and the tv-app StrokeCache copy of decimate. The TV draws radii in width units (ContentRect.w). So a circle dragged straight down is drawn 1.78x the dragged size, and one dragged at 45 degrees is 1.44x. The phone's own preview (pixel hypot, companion:388) shows the correct ring, so the phone and the TV disagree. The eraser misses the top and bottom of every ring with a radius over 0.032. It grabs empty air inside a ring. It cannot reach the upper and lower 44% of a spotlight. Its tolerance band is 56% as tall as it is wide. The HitTest docstring promises the opposite. The move is structural rather than nine patches: a Metric(aspect) value in core owns distance, pointToSegment and the decimation test. HitTest.pick and Smoothing.decimate take it, with no default, so the compiler finds every caller. PenEngine builds one from its own videoAspect. The planned name-tag snap (HitTest.kt:11) then inherits a correct metric instead of the bias.

## Flow
- Write MetricTest with cases 1-7 red against today's maths; case 8 is the existing suite
- Add Metric.kt (width-unit distance, point-to-segment, isotropic decimation test)
- HitTest.pick/distanceTo take a Metric; PenEngine passes Metric(videoAspect) to pick and uses it for circle/spotlight radius
- Smoothing.decimate takes the Metric; PenEngine's commit passes it
- Overlay StrokeCache decimates in pixel space (rect.w(0.004) against pixel distance), which is isotropic by construction
- Protocol.Erase.tolerance doc: a fraction of the picture width in every direction

## Expected impact
Circles and spotlights, 2 of the 6 tools, land on the TV where the finger drew them in every direction. The eraser grabs what the viewer sees. The phone preview and the TV agree. One rule replaces nine copies.

## Evaluation
Claim: every normalized distance in core is aspect-correct, and the circle drawn on the TV equals the drag
Before: 0 of 6 behaviour cases pass (cases 2 and 8 are GUARDs, green before); vertical-drag circle 192 px for a 108 px drag
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: none

HitTest.pick callers: PenEngine.kt:173 only. Arithmetic (aspect 16/9): vertical drag dyN=0.1 -> engine radius 0.1, true width-unit radius 0.1/1.7778=0.05625, drawn 0.1*1920=192 px vs dragged 0.1*1080=108 px. Ring top tap at dyN=r*a: |r*a - r| = 0.778r > 0.025 for r > 0.032. Existing tests re-checked under the new metric: stroke tap (0.5,0.51) 0.0056 hit; (0.5,0.9) 0.225 miss; ring (0.7,0.5) 0 hit; ring centre 0.2 miss; spotlight (0.95,0.95) hypot(0.45,0.253)-0.2 = 0.316 miss; arrow (0.2,0.15) 0.028 -> null at 0.01, hit at 0.1; eraser rows 0.3/0.7 are 0.1125 from the tap at 0.5 -> only the middle row erased.

cards.title: Edits you can see: Clear cleans this frame, off-screen undo takes you there
acceptance: case 1: engine with a Stroke at 5_000, an Arrow at 5_200 and a Stroke at 12_000 (default 6 s hold); accept(PenMessage.ClearFrame, 5_300) -> the doc holds only the 12_000 stroke and AnnotationTimeline(doc).moments() == [12_000] (JUnit :core:test, VisibleEditsTest)

case 2: after case 1, accept(Undo, 5_300) -> the three annotations return with ids in their original order [a1, a2, a3] (a new Op that restores several at their indices, not ClearAll) (JUnit :core:test)

case 3: GUARD: decodePenMessage('{"type":"clear"}') still clears every moment and one Undo restores all of them - the remote's D-pad Down (MainActivity.kt:130) and the harness clean slate (live-ui-test.mjs:72-76, relay-test.mjs:211) depend on it (JUnit :core:test)

case 4: strokes at 12_000 then 5_000; engine.undoAt(15_000) == 5_000 and TransportPlan.plan('undo', positionMs = 15_000, undoAtMs = 5_000) == [Pause, SeekTo(5_000)] with annotationCount unchanged; at 5_000, undoAt(5_000) == null and plan('undo', positionMs = 5_000) == [Edit(Undo)] (JUnit :core:test)
case 5: after that undo, with the playhead at 15_000, engine.redoAt(15_000) == 5_000 and plan('redo', positionMs = 15_000, redoAtMs = 5_000) == [Pause, SeekTo(5_000)] (JUnit :core:test)

case 6: GUARD: an undo whose target is on screen stays one press - plan('undo') == [Edit(Undo)] (ReviewModeTest.kt:86 unchanged), undoAt(t) == null when the target is visible at t, and undoAt is null when the next op is a whole-clip ClearAll (JUnit :core:test)

case 7: the phone's undo takes the planner's road - PenMessage.Undo.asTransport() == Transport('undo'), Redo -> Transport('redo'), and ClearFrame, Clear and Pen -> null (Session.accept routes on it) (JUnit :core:test)
case 8: HeartbeatInput(undoAtMs = 5_000) -> the state JSON contains "undoAtMs":5000; with null the key is absent and the JSON has no 'null' (HeartbeatTest case 8 guard holds) (JUnit :core:test)

cards.rollback: Four commits (core tests, core ops/plan/state, tv-app routing, companion buttons + README). The wire change is additive: a new message type 'clearFrame' and two optional State fields that an older phone ignores (ignoreUnknownKeys). Reverting the series restores the old Clear, Undo and Redo exactly, and nothing is persisted.
cards.runner_up: A review survives a relaunch: the TV saves the AnnotationDoc per clip and restores it with ids that continue (PenEngine.kt:48,72 restart ids at a1, and Overlay.kt:219-221 caches stroke geometry by id); direction gate.
cards.body:
## Summary
Review mode turned a clip into a row of drawn moments. Clear still wipes all of them in one press of the remote's Down key, and Undo removes ink on a frame the viewer is not looking at, so the loss is invisible. The eraser already refuses to reach through time. Make every edit obey the same rule. Clear cleans the frame on screen (Clear all stays one explicit button, and the remote keeps its clean-slate meaning). An undo or redo whose ink is on another frame first takes the TV there, paused, and the next press acts. The phone labels Undo with where it will go.

## Description
The data is already in core. History holds the op, the op holds the annotation, and the annotation holds its frame. The engine is handed the media time on every accept. None of it is used. Changes:
- History gains peek and a RemoveSet op (several annotations restored at their indices).
- PenEngine gains ClearFrame (remove what visibleAt(t) shows, one undoable op) and undoAt(t)/redoAt(t), the frame the next edit acts on, or null when it is on screen or whole-clip.
- TransportPlan turns an off-screen undo or redo into [Pause, SeekTo(frame)].
- The phone's Undo and Redo are routed through the same planner as the remote's (PenMessage.asTransport), which closes the two-road split.
- State carries undoAtMs and redoAtMs, so the phone's button reads 'Undo - 5.0s' before it travels, instead of acting blind.
Wire (contract), additive: {type:'clearFrame'}, and State.undoAtMs/redoAtMs are optional and omitted when null. Consumers: companion/index.html (sends clearFrame from Clear, clear from a new Clear all, reads undoAtMs/redoAtMs). tv-app Session.kt (routes Undo/Redo, fills HeartbeatInput), MainActivity.kt (passes undoAtMs/redoAtMs to plan), PenSessionHost.kt (unchanged, Deliver). tools/live-ui-test.mjs (same-frame undo/redo/erase checks unchanged, plus one new off-screen check), tools/relay-test.mjs (D-pad clear unchanged), tools/relay-stub.mjs (forwards unread; /health spreads the new fields), tools/pen-sim.mjs and tools/latency-probe.mjs (send hello/transport/pen/shape/ping only; unaffected).

## Flow
- The viewer builds 8 moments and sits on moment 3.
- Clear: moment 3's ink goes, and moments 1-2 and 4-8 stay (the tick for moment 3 leaves the scrub bar).
- Undo: moment 3 comes back in place.
- Undo again, when the last drawing was at moment 8: the button read 'Undo - 38.2s', and the TV pauses on moment 8 with that ink visible.
- Undo once more: that drawing goes, on screen.
- The remote's Down still clears the clip, as the harness expects.

## Expected impact
No edit changes ink the viewer cannot see. One accidental Clear costs one frame, not the whole walk-through. Undo becomes a way to walk back through your own work. Every edit in the pen experience now follows the rule the eraser already enforces.

## Evaluation
Claim: clear, undo and redo never change a frame that is not on screen, and the phone knows before it presses
Before: 0 of 6 behaviour cases pass (cases 3 and 6 are GUARDs, green before); 3 of 4 edit kinds (clear, undo, redo) reach off screen, and 2 roads for undo
After: 8 of 8; 0 of 4 edit kinds reach off screen; 1 road
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first; the live-ui-test journey needs a device (emulator or Stick) and is reported separately
Result: better
Gate: contract
